text:
alex: quick alert from canary-us-east-2: observed a sudden collapse in prefix/prompt-cache hit-rate after yesterday's kernel-selector rollout.

maria: numbers?

alex: runtime-canary-3. Prefix hit went from ~81% down to ~31% over ~2h. p50 gen latency +9ms, p95 +26ms, throughput -10%.

kevin: kernel-selector change shouldn't touch keying. Any coincident commits?

maria: there was a small PR to strip tenant identifiers from logs. Looks like the change ended up altering the cache key construction. Snippet from the image: 

```
# compact keying: removed tenant
h = blake3((prefix + model + seq).encode()).hexdigest()[:20]
```

maria: we truncated the digest and removed tenant_id from the preimage to avoid exposing tenant in logs. Combined effect: higher collision rate across tenants.

sara: do we encrypt cache entries by tenant?

alex: encryption is per-shard AES with a shared key. So same cache key -> same ciphertext -> can be served to any tenant.

megan: bad combo. I ran a short warmup experiment in the lab (2 tenants, similar prompt families). We prewarmed ~4.8k keys per tenant and saw 98 collisions (2.0%). In the canary run, sampling shows ~1.8% of served warmup hits came from another tenant's cached outputs.

kevin: immediate actions:
- disable serving from prefix-cache on shared pools (feature-flag)
- roll back canary kernel-selector to the previous image
- patch key derivation to include tenant-specific HMAC
- rotate cache encryption key + invalidate recent entries
- run an audit for cross-tenant serves in the last 72h

maria: minimal safe keying I propose (temporary):
```
def cache_key(tenant_id, prefix, model, seq):
    k = kms.get('cache-hmac')
    return hmac.new(k, f\"{tenant_id}|{prefix}|{model}|{seq}\".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
```
I'll open a PR with unit tests for collision prob and an integration test asserting tenant separations.

alex: I'll toggle the prefix-cache-serving feature flag and enqueue a rollback.

deploy-bot: rollback queued: runtime-canary-3 -> revert/kernel-selector (sha:aa11bb). ETA 6m.

ops-bot: Can confirm feature-flag set: shared-prefix-cache-serving=false on clusters: runtime-canary-3, runtime-canary-4.

maria: after flags and rollback we should plan a safe rewarm strategy: re-run warmup per-tenant once new keying lands, don't rely on prior entries.

kevin: also: add CI lint that rejects cache-key functions that don't accept tenant input or that truncate digests below a safety threshold (e.g., <96 bits).

megan: security note: even if ciphertext is opaque, content-level responses from tenant A served to tenant B = confidentiality breach. Escalating.

sec-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-118. Severity: High. Security on-call paged.

alex: quick audit snapshot: scanned warmup logs for the canary window (6h) -> 214 cross-tenant serves across 73 tenants. That's canary-only sample, not prod.

maria: I'll add anonymized instrumentation to log (tenant_hash, cache_key) on cache hits that differ from request tenant so we can quantify without storing payloads.

kevin: pragmatic mitigation options:
- short-term: per-tenant cache namespaces (prepend tenant -> cheap)
- medium: per-tenant envelope encryption using tenant KMS material
- long-term: strong testing harness that simulates multi-tenant warmup collisions before rollout

megan: legal/security asked for disclosure guidance. Sara, can you draft a customer-facing timeline after we know scope?

sara: yup. I'll coordinate with legal. For now label remediation ETA: revert done + keying PR in flight within 2h, canary verification within 3h, broader rollout blocked until audit completes.

maria: PR up with HMAC keying + tests. Also added an integration test that intentionally runs two tenants warming identical prefix families and asserts zero cross-tenant hits.

alex: post-rollback stats: after revert in canary we saw prefix hit-rate recover to ~79% within 25m. That confirms kernel-selector change correlated with the symptom but root cause is keying change included in the same deploy.

kevin: after we land the keying patch we'll need a cache invalidation plan: invalidate all entries generated in the last 72h on shared shards and rewarm per-tenant to restore hit-rate.

maria: scheduling invalidation job: will mark affected shards and rotate AES key as part of the maintenance window. Rewarm will be scheduled to avoid traffic spikes.

megan: for audits, I recommend scanning both warmup logs and live cache-hit logs for the last 7 days once instrumentation is live, to ensure we didn't miss earlier rollouts.

alex: owners: maria -> PR + tests + rewarm plan; kevin -> CI lint + key-entropy rule; megan -> audit sampling + coord w/ security; sara -> incident lead + disclosure.

maria: pushing small patch now. Will post PR link.

alex: thanks everyone. We'll reconvene here after PR merges and canary validates. I'll start a short postmortem draft once audit numbers stabilize.

[link] https://internal.perf/dash/1767777000-prefixcache-incident (canary graphs + warmup diffs)
